Michael John Reimer's 1989 Georgetown PhD is listed as Administration and Society in Alexandria, Egypt, 1807–1882.
A 1986–87 fellowship listing places Michael Reimer at Georgetown researching Alexandria, 1798–1882.

basis: The review says the book was based on Reimer's doctoral thesis; a 1989 Georgetown dissertation listing and a contemporaneous fellowship listing connect Reimer to the corresponding Alexandria research. The dissertation is listed under a different title, so the link to the AHA title is inferred.

evidence.says: Robert C. Binkley's timeline lists his 1927 Stanford dissertation on European public opinion and Wilson and his 1935 book Realism and Nationalism.
The library catalogue credits Realism and nationalism, 1852-1871 to Robert Cedric Binkley, 1897-1940.

basis: The timeline identifies both the dissertation on side b and the book on side a as works of Robert C. Binkley. The library catalogue identifies the book's author as Robert Cedric Binkley.

evidence.says: Charly Coleman is a Columbia history professor and author of The Virtues of Abandon; he was an Institute member in 2017–2018.
Charly Coleman of Columbia University authored the 2018 review of The Great Demarcation.
Charly J. Coleman earned a Stanford Ph.D. in 2005 and wrote The Virtues of Abandon.

basis: The 2018 review identifies its author at Columbia, where the author of The Virtues of Abandon was a history professor in the same period. Columbia also identifies the book author as holding a 2005 Stanford Ph.D., consistent with the thesis record.

evidence.says: Sandra Moats wrote Celebrating the Republic and Navigating Neutrality and received a history doctorate from UCLA in 2001.
Sandra A. Moats earned a history PhD at UCLA in 2001 with the dissertation The Last Republican: James Monroe's Tours and the Politics of Succession.

basis: The author of both books and the author of the thesis share the same history doctorate at UCLA in 2001. This specific degree and year connect the two records.
